notes: Eight own pages read; seven HTTP 200 and not thin, the trust center (trust.alvys.com, redirecting to a Drata trust page) answered HTTP 403 and is listed for a browser read; it would settle the SOC 2 claim (C28). Pass 2 (8 Oct): browser-reads.json requested trust.alvys.com, but the manifest has no browser row for Alvys, so no claim could be re-classed from a browser read and the URL stays in needs_browser_read; the fetch tool was not used again (the trust page was already read once and no other alvys.com page mentions SOC 2). The pricing page carries no dollar figures, so every dollar starting price (C08 to C12) and the quote-only and published-pricing claims (C13, C14) are unverifiable rather than true or wrong. C25 (mobile app browser-based) is classed wrong on the home page's Install Alvys Driver App and the driver app page; the raw home HTML links that line to App Store and Google Play listings for the Alvys driver app. Pass 2 consistency check: C25 is the only wrong claim and stays wrong (same subject, explicit on the vendor's own pages); a reviewer may still ask whether the answer's 'Mobile App' row meant office-user access rather than the driver app. Pass 2 completeness: one claim added, C30 (120+ ELD integrations, q8 Claude run 2 table cell), unverifiable; the other gap lines and table cells repeat claims already coded for the same answers ($299, $514, $292, $183, unlimited users, contracts, 120+ integrations, driver app) or are positioning, ratings, funding, feature lines (native EDI, IFTA, accounting integrations with no named product) or hedged or attributed lines ('around $300/mo' as a buyer budget, 'published figures ... in some comparisons', 'Setup Fees | Varies'). Cause trace for C25: four of the answer's cited pages read (softwareconnect.com and tentrucks.com do not carry the statement; bestguide.com and g2.com answered HTTP 403), so cause not found. Out of scope and not coded: the $40M Series B and other funding, review ratings, the 22% load growth and 9% revenue figures, and the hedged lines (typically flat-rate, typically unlimited office users, Setup Fees Varies). The integrations page lists MyCarrierPortal, not MyCarrierPackets, so C24 stays unverifiable.
